concerns: The proposed national contrast is weak because berkunjung and melawat are both ordinary visit terms in Malaysian Malay, and melawat is also available in Indonesian.
cal2-social-001:social-06.cue_rationale: Both answers fit going to see someone socially.
cal2-social-001:social-06.rationale: The answers share the intended social-visit sense, but the pairing overstates a national lexical distinction.
cal2-social-001:social-06.shared_synonym_rationale: Berku​​njung is ordinary in Malaysian Malay and melawat is an established Indonesian form, even if berkunjung is the clearer Indonesian default.

cal2-social-001:social-07.cue_rationale: Both answers fit spending informal social time with others.
cal2-social-001:social-07.rationale: Nongkrong and lepak are clear colloquial choices for informal socializing in Indonesian and Malaysian Malay respectively.
cal2-social-001:social-07.shared_synonym_rationale: No shared everyday synonym was identified that materially weakens this colloquial Indonesian–Malaysian preference.

cal2-social-001:social-08.cue_rationale: Both answers directly express saying one is sorry.
cal2-social-001:social-08.rationale: Both forms ordinarily mean to apologize; minta maaf is more colloquial, while memohon maaf is more formal.
cal2-social-001:social-08.risk_rationale: The main contrast is register rather than a strict national vocabulary split.

cal2-social-001:social-09.cue_rationale: Both forms describe feeling sure of one's abilities or judgment.
cal2-social-001:social-09.rationale: Percaya diri is the ordinary Indonesian preference, while yakin diri is a credible ordinary Malaysian preference for feeling confident.
cal2-social-001:social-09.risk_rationale: Cross-border comprehension and occasional borrowing may reduce the contrast in some contexts.
cal2-social-001:social-09.shared_synonym_rationale: Percaya diri is also understood and used in Malaysia, but yakin diri remains a useful Malaysian preference; the forms are not exclusive.

concerns: The proposed Malaysian form is not a reliable ordinary counterpart for disappointed in this neutral cue.
cal2-social-001:social-10.cue_rationale: A concise cue cannot ensure the same ordinary sense for hampa without adding a different emotional nuance.
material_concerns: Hampa is more strongly associated with empty, hollow, or unfulfilled meanings in Indonesian and is not a dependable national alternative to kecewa for this sense.
cal2-social-001:social-10.rationale: Kecewa fits the sense in both countries, whereas hampa is a marked or context-dependent choice and can shift the meaning toward emotional emptiness or frustration.
cal2-social-001:social-10.shared_synonym_rationale: Kecewa is also ordinary in Malaysia and would commonly defeat hampa for the neutral sense of disappointed.

cal2-travel-001:travel-01.cue_rationale: Both answers directly denote an aircraft used for air travel.
cal2-travel-001:travel-01.rationale: Pesawat is the ordinary Indonesian preference and kapal terbang the ordinary Malaysian preference for an airplane.
cal2-travel-001:travel-01.risk_rationale: Pesawat is not unknown in Malaysia, so the national preference is not exclusive.
cal2-travel-001:travel-01.shared_synonym_rationale: Pesawat is understood and used in Malaysia, especially in formal or technical contexts, but kapal terbang remains a useful everyday Malaysian preference.

cal2-travel-001:travel-02.cue_rationale: Both answers denote a place where buses stop for passengers.
cal2-travel-001:travel-02.rationale: Halte is the ordinary Indonesian term, while perhentian bas is the standard Malaysian term for a bus stop.
cal2-travel-001:travel-02.risk_rationale: Informal cross-border usage may make halte recognizable to some Malaysian speakers.
cal2-travel-001:travel-02.shared_synonym_rationale: Halte may be understood in Malaysia through Indonesian usage but is not the usual standard Malaysian term; perhentian bas is the ordinary local choice.

concerns: Indonesian jalan tol specifically means toll road, a subtype of highway.
cal2-travel-001:travel-03.cue_rationale: No concise neutral cue preserves the broad highway sense while making jalan tol and lebuh raya equivalent.
material_concerns: The candidate mismatches the exact sense by pairing a subtype with the broader English category.
cal2-travel-001:travel-03.rationale: Lebuh raya is a highway, while jalan tol is specifically a toll road; the proposed answers do not express the same exact concept.

cal2-travel-001:travel-04.cue_rationale: Both answers denote the condition in which traffic moves very slowly or stops.
cal2-travel-001:travel-04.rationale: Kemacetan and kesesakan lalu lintas are ordinary Indonesian and Malaysian terms for a traffic jam.

cal2-travel-001:travel-05.cue_rationale: Both answers fit a planned timetable of transport times.
cal2-travel-001:travel-05.rationale: Jadwal and jadual are the regular Indonesian and Malaysian forms, differing mainly in spelling.

cal2-travel-001:travel-06.cue_rationale: Both answers denote the act of reaching a destination.
cal2-travel-001:travel-06.rationale: Kedatangan is the ordinary Indonesian term, while ketibaan is the standard Malaysian term for arrival.
cal2-travel-001:travel-06.risk_rationale: Malaysian usage may vary between ketibaan and kedatangan by context and register.
cal2-travel-001:travel-06.shared_synonym_rationale: Kedatangan also occurs in Malaysian general contexts, but ketibaan is a credible standard transport/formal preference there.

cal2-travel-001:travel-07.cue_rationale: The travel context disambiguates tujuan as the place someone is traveling to, and both answers fit that sense.
cal2-travel-001:travel-07.rationale: Tujuan is the ordinary Indonesian choice for destination in this context, while destinasi is highly common in Malaysian travel usage.
cal2-travel-001:travel-07.risk_rationale: Both alternatives are understood across the border, so the contrast is preferential rather than exclusive.
cal2-travel-001:travel-07.shared_synonym_rationale: Destinasi is also used in Indonesian and tujuan is understood in Malaysian, but the proposed forms remain useful ordinary national/contextual preferences for travel destinations.

cal2-travel-001:travel-08.cue_rationale: The cue directly expresses the shared travel-ticket sense.
cal2-travel-001:travel-08.rationale: Both forms naturally mean a ticket for travel in one direction only; sekali jalan is the ordinary Indonesian preference and sehala the Malaysian preference.
cal2-travel-001:travel-08.shared_synonym_rationale: Satu arah or satu hala may be understood, but sekali jalan and sehala are the more useful ordinary choices in the respective locales.

cal2-travel-001:travel-09.cue_rationale: The cue clearly identifies the return-travel ticket sense.
cal2-travel-001:travel-09.rationale: Both forms naturally mean a ticket covering travel to a destination and back; pulang-pergi is ordinary Indonesian usage and pergi balik is ordinary Malaysian usage.
cal2-travel-001:travel-09.shared_synonym_rationale: Pulang-pergi may be understood in Malaysia and pergi balik may be understood in Indonesia, but each is notably less preferred there than the proposed local form.

cal2-travel-001:travel-10.cue_rationale: Both answers fit the place where roads meet.
cal2-travel-001:travel-10.rationale: Persimpangan is the ordinary Indonesian term, while simpang is a common Malaysian everyday term for a road junction or intersection.
cal2-travel-001:travel-10.risk_rationale: Cross-border use of simpang in Indonesian and persimpangan in Malaysian formal contexts may merit later usage review.
cal2-travel-001:travel-10.shared_synonym_rationale: Simpang also occurs in Indonesian, especially in compounds such as simpang tiga or simpang empat, and persimpangan is understood in Malaysia; nevertheless, the proposed forms teach a credible everyday preference.

cal2-work-001:work-01.cue_rationale: Colleague directly matches the shared workplace-person sense.
cal2-work-001:work-01.rationale: Rekan kerja and rakan sekerja are closely corresponding ordinary forms for a person who works with you, with useful Indonesian–Malaysian lexical and spelling differences.

cal2-work-001:work-03.cue_rationale: Grade can also mean a level, rank, or school year; schoolwork score makes the intended sense explicit for both answers.
cal2-work-001:work-03.rationale: Nilai is the ordinary Indonesian term for a schoolwork score or evaluation, while markah is the ordinary Malaysian term for the score received.
cal2-work-001:work-03.shared_synonym_rationale: Skor is understood in both countries, but nilai and markah remain the more locally characteristic ordinary terms for this educational sense.

cal2-work-001:work-04.cue_rationale: School break can also suggest a vacation; school recess precisely matches both answers.
cal2-work-001:work-04.rationale: Istirahat is ordinary Indonesian and rehat is ordinary Malaysian Malay for a school recess or break.
cal2-work-001:work-04.risk_rationale: School break is mildly ambiguous between recess and vacation.
cal2-work-001:work-04.shared_synonym_rationale: No relevant competing shared synonym weakens the national preference.

cal2-work-001:work-05.cue_rationale: Both answers directly denote a room used by teachers at a school.
cal2-work-001:work-05.rationale: Ruang guru is the ordinary Indonesian term, while bilik guru is the ordinary Malaysian Malay term for a teachers’ room.
cal2-work-001:work-05.shared_synonym_rationale: No relevant shared synonym concern was identified.

cal2-work-001:work-06.cue_rationale: Both answers fit a period of practical work experience, especially in an education or workplace context.
cal2-work-001:work-06.rationale: Magang is the ordinary Indonesian term; latihan industri is an ordinary formal Malaysian term for an internship or practical industry placement.
cal2-work-001:work-06.risk_rationale: Latihan industri is especially associated with student or industry placements, while internship is broader in some contexts.
cal2-work-001:work-06.shared_synonym_rationale: Internship is also used as a borrowing in Malaysia, but latihan industri remains a credible formal and educational preference; this does not defeat the contrast.

cal2-work-001:work-07.cue_rationale: Both answers directly denote required school or workplace clothing.
cal2-work-001:work-07.rationale: Seragam is the ordinary Indonesian form, while uniform is a common ordinary Malaysian Malay form for required clothing.
cal2-work-001:work-07.shared_synonym_rationale: Pakaian seragam is understood and used in both countries, including formal contexts, but seragam versus uniform still teaches a useful ordinary national preference.

cal2-work-001:work-08.cue_rationale: Tarikh akhir specifically denotes a final calendar date, whereas the original latest time can imply a precise time of day.
cal2-work-001:work-08.rationale: Tenggat waktu is the ordinary Indonesian term, while tarikh akhir is the ordinary Malaysian Malay term for the final date or deadline.
cal2-work-001:work-08.risk_rationale: Tarikh akhir is date-focused, while tenggat waktu can cover a date or a precise time.
cal2-work-001:work-08.shared_synonym_rationale: Deadline is also used as a common borrowing in both countries, especially informally or professionally, but the proposed local terms remain useful ordinary preferences.

cal2-work-001:work-10.cue_rationale: Both answers fit the same document sense without narrowing.
cal2-work-001:work-10.rationale: Indonesian sertifikat and Malaysian sijil are ordinary forms for an official document confirming achievement or completion.
cal2-work-001:work-10.shared_synonym_rationale: Sertifikat is understood in Malaysia but sijil is the ordinary established Malay term; sijil is not the ordinary Indonesian preference for this sense.
